cards.explanation: The answer is that she would come back to Him. God says, "I thought that after she had done all these things, she would return to Me." (Jeremiah 3:7) Hills, trees, the whole tour, and He still figured she'd come home. Keep that in your pocket, friends, because the whole passage keeps coming back to this.

The answer is a certificate of divorce. God says, "…I gave her a certificate of divorce and sent her away." (Jeremiah 3:8) It happened because faithless Israel had committed adultery. That's the paper in this verse.

The answer is False. Judah watched Israel get sent away, and the text says she "…had no fear and prostituted herself as well." (Jeremiah 3:8) She saw it all happen and kept going anyway. That's one stubborn sister.

The answer is pretense. God says Judah "…did not return to Me with all her heart, but only in pretense…" (Jeremiah 3:10) That's like a person who shows up to the kitchen in an apron and never touches the dough. The look was there. The heart wasn't, all the way.

The answer is True. The LORD tells Jeremiah, "Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than unfaithful Judah." (Jeremiah 3:11) Hear that again slowly, friends. Israel, the one who got sent away, comes out looking better than Judah.

The answer is merciful. God says, "I will no longer look on you with anger, for I am merciful…" (Jeremiah 3:12) That's God's own reason, right there in His words. And He adds, "I will not be angry forever." Say that one out loud, friends.

The answer is to admit her guilt. God says, "Only acknowledge your guilt, that you have rebelled against the LORD your God." (Jeremiah 3:13) Notice that word "only." No receipt, no apology tour, just own it. Easier said than done, I know.

The answer is knowledge and understanding. God says, "Then I will give you shepherds after My own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding." (Jeremiah 3:15) That's a different kind of meal, friends. These shepherds feed people what they need to know. And I love that He calls them shepherds after His own heart.

The answer is True. God says, "It will never come to mind, and no one will remember it or miss it, nor will another one be made." (Jeremiah 3:16) He's talking about "those days," when they multiply and increase in the land. I'll leave it right at His words, and I won't guess past them.

The answer is The Throne of the LORD. God says, "At that time they will call Jerusalem The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations will be gathered in Jerusalem to honor the name of the LORD." (Jeremiah 3:17) That's a new name for the city. And look at who's coming: all the nations.

The answer is True. God says of that time, "They will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts." (Jeremiah 3:17) That's part of what He says about that time. It's a promise for the days ahead.

The answer is Israel. "In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and they will come together from the land of the north…" (Jeremiah 3:18) Remember those two unfaithful sisters? Now they're walking together. I'd pay good money to see that family reunion.

The answer is Father. God says, "I thought you would call Me 'Father' and never turn away from following Me." (Jeremiah 3:19) That's what He had in mind for them. It comes right after He says He longs to make them His sons. Friends, I read that line and I sit down for a minute.

The answer is that they had turned away and forgotten the LORD. The text says they are weeping and begging for mercy "…because they have perverted their ways and forgotten the LORD their God." (Jeremiah 3:21) That's the reason it gives. A voice heard on the barren heights, and it's the sound of people who know it.

The answer is that He will heal it. God says, "Return, O faithless children, and I will heal your faithlessness." (Jeremiah 3:22) Heal, friends. Not just point at it, but fix it. That's an invitation worth saying yes to.

The answer is False. The people say deception comes from the hills and commotion from the mountains. Then comes the line that counts: "Surely the salvation of Israel is in the LORD our God." (Jeremiah 3:23) They finally know where to look.

The answer is both they and their fathers. The people say, "We have sinned against the LORD our God, both we and our fathers…" (Jeremiah 3:25) Nobody points a finger at somebody else. They say we, and they say our fathers. That's owning it, friends.

The answer is True. The people say it themselves: "from our youth even to this day we have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God." (Jeremiah 3:25) No dodging and no excuses. I think that's hard to say out loud.

The answer is their idols. God says, "If you will remove your detestable idols from My sight and no longer waver…" (Jeremiah 4:1) That's what He names to remove from His sight. And it begins with an "if," so it's an open door.

The answer is nations. God says, "…then the nations will be blessed by Him, and in Him they will glory." (Jeremiah 4:2) The blessing reaches the nations, not just Israel. That's a big blessing hanging on a small word like "if."
The answer is their hearts. God says, "Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and remove the foreskins of your hearts…" (Jeremiah 4:4) It's the heart He names, the inside. Not just the outside, friends.

The answer is False. God says, "Otherwise, My wrath will break out like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it, because of your evil deeds." (Jeremiah 4:4) Nothing in that says it flares for a moment and passes. I think it's a heavy verse, and it's a good reason to listen to that word return.
